headline: Deputy Minister Fawaz Al Shora Opens Big 5 Construct Saudi in Riyadh
deck: Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources patronage places the Kingdom's largest construction show inside the localisation policy frame.
excerpt: Eng Fawaz bin Badr Al Shora, Deputy Minister of Industry and Mineral Resources for Industrial Services and Compliance, opened Big 5 Construct Saudi 2026 at Riyadh Front. The ministry's patronage places the four-day exhibition inside a policy frame of industrial licensing, product compliance and local content rules that have tightened through 2026.
content:
Eng Fawaz bin Badr Al Shora, Deputy Minister of Industry and Mineral Resources for Industrial Services and Compliance, opened Big 5 Construct Saudi 2026 in Riyadh on Sunday, the largest construction event staged in the Kingdom and one held this year under the patronage of his ministry.

The show runs for four days at the Riyadh Front Exhibition and Conference Center at ROSHN Front, with more than 1,000 exhibitors from over 50 countries and an organiser expectation of upwards of 35,000 trade visitors. Its sector coverage spans general construction, concrete, heavy equipment, HVACR and facilities management, carried across four co-located exhibitions: Heavy Saudi Arabia, Totally Concrete Saudi Arabia, HVACR Saudi Arabia and Saudi FM & Clean.

Ministry patronage places the event inside a specific policy frame. The Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources is the body that issues industrial licences, oversees factory registration and administers much of the machinery through which Saudi Arabia is attempting to build domestic manufacturing depth under the National Industrial Development and Logistics Program. A construction supply-chain exhibition is one of the few places where the output of that policy is physically assembled in a single venue, from admixtures and fireproofing to castings, block plant, structural steel and chillers.

The department Al Shora leads, industrial services and compliance, is also the part of the ministry closest to the questions that dominate a buying floor. Compliance covers product conformity, standards and the regulatory obligations that determine whether a manufactured item can be supplied into a Saudi project at all. For an exhibition where a large share of the value on display is certified building product, that is not a ceremonial fit.

The industrial base the ministry supervises has expanded quickly. Saudi Arabia counted 13,660 active industrial facilities at the end of April 2026, an increase of more than 11 per cent on the 12,289 recorded a year earlier. In April alone the ministry issued 322 new industrial licences tied to investment above SAR 12.33 billion and projected to create more than 2,900 jobs, while 188 factories entered production during the month with investment above SAR 2 billion.

Procurement policy has been moving in step. The Local Content and Government Procurement Authority, established at the end of 2018, applies a minimum local content threshold of 40 per cent to public tenders and maintains a national product mandatory list for government buying. In February 2026 the authority introduced and phased in higher minimum local content percentages for products on that list, tightening the requirement on state purchasers and, by extension, on the supply chains serving them.

Those two forces, a rapidly growing licensed factory base and procurement rules that reward domestic content, largely explain the composition of this week's exhibitor list. Saudi manufacturers occupy a substantial share of the floor across construction chemicals, passive fire protection, steel products, precast and block-making equipment, and air-conditioning plant, in most cases presenting production capacity inside the Kingdom rather than distribution arrangements.

The demand side gives the policy its urgency. Saudi construction output is forecast to grow 6.2 per cent this year to around SAR 232.14 billion, and monthly contract awards recorded by the Saudi Contractors Authority reached SR 30.03 billion across 18 projects in May, the year's highest by value, followed by 25 awards worth more than SR 29.5 billion in June. Sustaining that volume with imported material carries lead-time and currency exposure that a domestic supply base is intended to reduce.

Big 5 Construct Saudi runs at Riyadh Front until 2 September, with a conference programme covering codes and standards, health and safety, sustainability, artificial intelligence, project management, concrete, modular construction and HVACR alongside the exhibition halls.
